body: After touching ~21,000 in Nov 2010 the Sensex went sideways-to-down for three years: ~15,100 in Dec 2011 (approximate) and a taper-tantrum low near ~18,000 in Aug 2013, while small caps fell much more (BSE Smallcap roughly -40% in 2011; unverified). Causes: inflation near double digits and 13 RBI rate hikes in 2010-11 (from memory), 'policy paralysis' and corruption scandals (2G, coal), stalled projects that later became bank NPAs, a current-account deficit near ~4.8% of GDP in FY13. On 22 May 2013 the Fed signalled tapering; Indian markets sold off - the Sensex fell 12% in 20 sessions from July, and on 16 Aug 2013 it fell 3.97% (769 points) to 18,598 and the Nifty 4.08% to 5,507.85, the biggest daily fall since 2011. The rupee lost almost 15% between 22 May and 30 Aug 2013, hitting a record ~68.8/USD on 28 Aug 2013 (from memory; sources found cite 62-64 mid-August). RBI tightened abruptly; Raghuram Rajan took over in Sept 2013 and the FCNR(B) deposit swap rebuilt reserves. Leaders: IT, pharma, FMCG (dollar earners, defensives); laggards: infra, PSU banks, realty, capital goods. Bottom signals: rupee capitulation plus forceful policy response, maximum pessimism, mid/small caps at multi-year low valuations (P/B near ~1 for many). Lesson: currency crises mark bottoms when policy credibly responds.
title: 2010-13 stagnation and the 2013 taper tantrum
